transcript: Welcome to my 2024 Theater Wrapped. I attended the theater 140 times in New York this year so I wanted to share with you some stats about what I saw and my overall theater going habits for the year. Starting off with when I was going to the theater, by month it looked like I went the most in October followed shortly by April and November. And then for days of the week, Sunday and Saturday were the most frequent time that I was going. And then for time of day almost 80% of the time I was going in the evening as opposed to a matinee. As far as where I was going, only about 40% of the times I went to the theater was to a Broadway theater and then about 60% of the times it was off Broadway which I think makes sense because there's always so many new shows funnelling through the off Broadway scene. Another 40/60 ratio is my plays versus musicals, where about 60% of what I saw was a play. And if you break this down even further, about 50% of everything that I saw throughout the year was considered an original or new play. Something nice about living in New York is I feel like I hear about a lot of things before they're really getting a ton of buzz and so I actually try to take advantage and go to something early before it's getting really difficult to get tickets. So you can see here I actually went to a lot of previews, over 50% of all performances that I went to this year were previews, and then I have some regular performances, a few closing performances, and some first previews as well. I have this graph here called repeats vs new, as in new to me. So I saw 118 distinct productions in 2024. And so the other 22 times that I attended the theater was for something that I'd seen before. There were some shows that I saw even more than twice within the year of 2024. There are six productions that I had previously seen prior to 2024 which I then saw again in 2024, and then there are seven productions that I saw more than once within the year of 2024. As far as what I thought, I have this kind of rating scale that goes from like amazing, great, good, mixed, to not for me. And you can see that things are pretty overwhelmingly positive. But I do think that I'm able to kind of meet a production where it is and kind of get a sense of what they're trying to do and judge based on that but also I think this skews somewhat positive because I'm obviously more likely to go back and see something again if I thought it was very good. I go to the theater rather spontaneously and I think way more frequently than the average person, so this is who I went with and you can see roughly two thirds of the time that I'm going to the theater I'm going by myself. But the rest of the time is pretty evenly split between family members, friends, and my partner Paul. Attending this much theater is certainly an investment, so in terms of time, I created this graph that shows the number of acts for each production that I was seeing and there's actually a slight edge toward one acts as opposed to two acts. But there were also some productions which were three acts, and one extremely long four act production. So this meant that I was attending 210 total acts. If you assume that each act is approximately 75 minutes that means that I was actively watching a show for 15,750 minutes or roughly 263 hours or roughly 10.9 days. As far as financial investment into this habit of mine, I wanted to show you kind of the price range buckets that I'm spending for these tickets. And you can actually see the vast majority of my tickets are less than $100. Most of them fall between 20 and 39 dollars, which, a lot of that is me taking advantage of subsidized or accessible ticketing programs for young audiences or otherwise. And I also have had some $0 or free tickets which could be through invites, gifts, comps, that sort of thing. So my total spend for the year was $4,855 which I actually think is not that bad when you think about 140 shows. This brings the average ticket price to about thirty four dollars and sixty eight cents. A few miscellaneous fun facts — I was very unlucky with lotteries this year so I only attended the theater on a lottery win once but I did attend a show from a rush, either digital or in person, seven times, and I have also at the time of this recording have seen every Broadway show that is currently running. Thank you for tuning into my Theater Wrapped for 2024. If you're curious about my thoughts on any of these shows, I post reviews for almost everything that I see and I also just posted my list of top 10 favorite shows of 2024. Happy Holidays and I'll see you at the theater very soon.
reasoning: This is Tyler's 2024 Theater Wrapped - a statistical summary of his theater-going habits for the year covering 140 shows. While he mentions posting reviews for shows he sees, this particular video is entirely focused on attendance statistics, spending habits, and theater-going patterns rather than reviewing any specific show including 'Raw'.
